The sleeve it comes with has a large strap on it.

Stanley Adventure Stainless Fry Pan Camp Cook Set, 9 Piece Camping Cookware Mess Kit with Stainless Pan, Cooking Utensils, and Dishes This Stanley cookware camp set is of a nice quality food grade pro level stainless steel. The set is Sized for limited storage space in mind yet useable decent size… as well as for easily fitting on camp stoves. Car, Jeep or trailer camping. They stack/nest nicely & have well thought out details.
The 4 stars for ? Of lightweight.. because these are a heavy layered bottom pans to cook more evenly. .not one layer & a light weight pan type. The bottom is even & heavy, with flip up (& can detach)handles with a slide down ring to steady /keep handle locked in proper use. . Flip over for when storing. Lids doubles as a strainer & the pot lid also has a double use, can be used as lid on skillet plus it includes decent spoon, spatula set, they are snapped together easily & taken apart, stored in set with good size silicon Pot holders. The cutting board, lol.. until some breaking in time, can be challenging but is of a decent size, Appreciate you at least have a cutting surface included. I like the top bungie strap that keeps the whole set snuggly tight, so no rattling. Usually it’s only 2 of us at camp, except when we family Vaca camp with our grown kids.. this set is good but I do bring additional iron skillet for needed additional cooking needs.
Follow directions on seasoning.. use with enough oil or butter, use at a lower heat to stop sticking but cleans up easily if happens. Use a low heat with soapy water to soak some for stuck on foods. Outside of pots, you can try to help keep nicer, some say rub a soap on to help in clean up later but open flames will tarnish shinny new look. . & if using over one. Flame, over coals preferred. But it’s the way this set heats up & cooks that counts. Clean to keep build up of oils, etc off set. I’m pleased & will be using set hopefully for a long time. I caught my set on sale making this set a great deal. If deciding, go with this set, you won’t be disappointed.
text_fidelity_b: Stanley Adventure Stainless Fry Pan Camp Cook Set, 9 Piece Camping Cookware Mess Kit with Stainless Pan, Cooking Utensils, and Dishes

The LGG tires weigh 233g each (my actual measurements), compared to 478g for the stock Espoir Sport Reflect 700x30c tires. But once in, the stand held up, and it was really windy this weekend where I was too. The stand does come with 2 binder clips, but my suggestion would be to carry a lot more of the clips because we went through a lot of them.

The blue target backer suggests to not add targets under the half point line. Why? Because people who are not that accurate will shoot low and take out the stand's frame. This is exactly what happened with us. I would guess the frame is about 2 inches wide, and it took some shots and was holding up fine, but it finally got shot through. Our fault for having targets top and bottom on the target backer. You can either get this stand or try to make your own out of PVC pipe.

Carrom 510.01 Balance Board [[VIDEOID:cdea6a4f11cba6bceb8d6b8b83d8a0a6]] This is an awesome balance board! I bought it in 2004, and it has held up really well for the past 9 years. Amazon was out of stock for a couple of years, so I'm super glad that it's back in stock, so I can recommend it to my friends.

This board is different than other balance boards that I've used, and I really liked that. Even if you have another balance board, I'd recommend this one, too. It's probably most similar to skateboarding or snowboarding, but it will help your balance in any sport. It took me about three weeks to get to the point that I am today, but I started out super uncoordinated. You'll probably pick it up much faster. I thought it was a great balance board to learn on, too. I definitely felt a sense of accomplishment after I got my balance enough to stay up on it for a minute or two.

It says the weight limit is 300 lbs, but this is super sturdy. I think it would actually work anywhere up to a 400 pound person.

It's pretty simple. You just roll back and forth and balance on top of it. If you got really good at it, you could do tricks and turns, but I'm not good enough to do much more than roll back and forth. I feel like it's really good exercise, too, and you could use weights on it, too, if you got to be really good at it.

Pros:
+Works on any surface. I've used it mostly on carpet.
+Extremely sturdy. It would be very hard to break this.
+Helps you prepare your balance for any sport or activity
+Low impact, so you can use this even if you have sore joints
+After you get used to it, you could watch TV, play video games, or read a book while you're balancing

Cons:
-Very simple. You just roll back and forth.

Wald 582 Folding Rear Bicycle Basket I wanted to attach this to a pakrak rear rack and had problems because of the design of the rack. The vertical supports that attach near the wheel axel are wider than the top of the rack so the hardare provided would not work. Even if the reach had been long enough the hardware was not big enough to go around the tubing of the rack.

i solved the problem with wire ties and that solution seems plenty strong. If its not strong enough Ill use hose clamps.

The clasp is very difficult to use and really should be redesigned. Others have commented on this shortcoming of the design. I had to use vice grips to bend the clasp so it would be workable by hand. That, of course scratched the paint. The paint on the steel wire where the clasp is attached is thick enough to keep the clasp from rotating freely so it was necessary to open and close the clasp many times with pliers to get it working smoothly enough.

I had planned to buy a second one of these for the other side of my rack but now plan to buy a similar product from another manufacturer and will amend this review after I install the second rack.

Oct 1, 2018 I bought a Sunlite basked and installed it today. I consider the Sunlite basket to be a superior product and provided details on my review of that product.
text_fidelity_b: Wald 582 Folding Rear Bicycle Basket

It heated well, but jeez, why do I want to futz with a heating pad every single time I get up out of my chair?  This, being made for a chair is sitting and staying put just fine!  I am happy with this heated pad for a chair - indoors or out.

text_fidelity_a: THERABAND FlexBar, Tennis Elbow Therapy Bar, Relieve Tendonitis Pain & Improve Grip Strength, Resistance Bar for Golfers Elbow & Tendinitis, Green, Medium, Intermediate I love this flexbar for its application to different joint exercises as part of an everyday exercise regimen.  My wife and I were noticing difficulty in opening jars and I have been having cervical neck pain.  My orthopedic consultant recommended progressive exercise and my physical therapist pointed to this type of device  as being useful for wrist strengthening and flexibility as well as for other uses in mobilizing muscle groups.  How these types of exercises work is illustrated in a handy multi-page manual that now comes with this device.  I had not imagine the range ways to use such a simple flexar.  I worked my way through a bunch of different ones and they each had value.  Many reviewers seem to be looking for a quick-fix rehab application for this tool and they ignore the value of progressive resistance training.  We are not all at the same start point in strength or in a recovery program.  "Guys" are always looking to jump back in the middle with poor results or prolonged injury time.  I've had it proven to me that it pays to start slow and be patient.  Having worked on my wrists and fingers with other Theraband devices, I moved up to the green flexbar recently.  Time will tell if my over-55 joints will benefit from the even higher blue level of resistance.

text_fidelity_a:
MOUNTAINTOP Watreproof 3 Season Tents for Camping/2 Person Camping Tent/Backpacking Tents with Carry Bag This tent seems like a great value at first. But when you can't sleep because of water seeping in, then drive yourself mad trying to tear down the tent in the morning you'll regret not buying a real tent.

The only plus I can give to this tent is that it sets up super easily. But to be honest, it's not really that much better than just setting up any other tent. The mechanism they have to pop the tent open works. But you're adding a lot of weight and mechanical complexity to something that's not very difficult in the first place.

On to the negatives.

It's impossibly annoying to tear down. While the tent pops open easily, it's a total pain to close. All of the plastic arms will start popping out of the mechanism. There's 8 joints you need to pull and close, one by one. And then you have to figure out which way the thing actually closes. But there's so much tension in the arms attached to the central hub that if you don't do it just right everything starts popping out.

So instead of just popping your tent poles out of the ground and pulling them out of the tent, you have to tear apart and rebuild this complicated lever mechanism spring loaded hub thing in the middle of the woods. And that's after you got no sleep because there's water in your tent.

The rain fly doesn't cover nearly enough of the tent. So if there's any rain it will rain directly on the tent, where as I said above, water will start seeping through into the tent. not just a little dampness. We had actual puddles in the tent.

I've had $20 Walmart tents that did a better job than this thing. It's not worth the money. It's overly complicated. And worst of all it just doesn't provide adequate shelter.
text_fidelity_b: MOUNTAINTOP Watreproof 3 Season Tents for Camping/2 Person Camping Tent/Backpacking Tents with Carry Bag

Allen Sports Deluxe+ Locking Quick Release 4-Bike Carrier for 2 in. Hitch, Model 840QR, Black I purchased the Premier Locking Quick Release 4-Bike Carrier for 2" Hitch on Vehicles with Spare Tire, Model 400QR , Black.

I've used it 4 times since I've purchased it in early April. It was delivered within a week with my Prime membership. Very easy to assemble with great instructions, took less than 10 minutes. It is well made and everything fit together nicely. Easy to install on my previously existing hitch. I have a 2" hitch on my 2014 Ford F-150, and it fit perfectly in it. The locking feature is easy to use and keeps the rack snug in the hitch, no wobble or looseness, and with the key lock I can leave the rack in place while I ride knowing it won't get stolen. I purchased the carrier model for vehicles with a spare tire, and that allows me to lower or pivot/swivel the carrier, while still installed in the truck hitch, and be able to completely lower the tailgate of my truck without hitting the carrier.

It is very easy to mount bikes to it, the supports can adjust to fit various frames. Female bike frames - I'd suggest getting an adapter to cross between the seat stem base and the handlebar base. Those are less than $40, and it makes mounting them just as easy and keeps them better leveled on the carrier as a male frame bike. I've carried up to 3 adult size frame mountain bikes of varying weights, and the carrier was able to easily accommodate them and handle the load. Getting a 4th bike on the carrier would be no problems at all. The rubber straps very securely hold the bikes to the carrier. I carried 3 adult size mountain bikes on a 7 hour ride (one way) and they did not move a bit. It comes with a long binder-type strong nylon strap that you can thread between all the bike frames and around the carrier's main post to stop the bikes from swaying going down the road, but I suggest getting some velcro straps to secure the wheels to the bike frames so they don't spin going down the road. You can get a 12-pack for under $20.

Overall I am VERY happy with this purchase. Considering this carrier is about a third or so of the cost of big name brands such as Thule, Yakima, etc, I think it is a very good quality item and a great value.

text_fidelity_a:
Long Western to English Leather Girth Converters I have spent endless hours trying to figure out how to convert a western saddle and a hybrid Brisbane Aussie saddle that uses a traditional D ring for rigging. Trust me, there’s more products that convert an English to western rigging but I was determined to call Australia and known saddlery companies to see if any product exists. I hit pay dirt here at Amazon after seeing them advertised at Elite Saddleworks in AU. Seems they sell their converters here at Amazon and my search is over.

As far as the product goes, these converter straps are beautifully made with heavy quality leather and a nice solid buckling system. So simple to use. Quite frankly, I did not think I was going to be able to find a correct product to make the conversion but I am delighted that these are on the market for those riders who do not like the typical Western strapping system for cinching. I find using a traditional English/Australian girth with a buckling system to be much safer for the rider and the horse… And you do not have to dismount to make any adjustments if the saddle becomes loose or needs re-positioning due to the girth.

So let me save you hours of trouble if you’re the type that has the rings on your saddle for cinching and you want to go to a buckled girth. My other suggestion is I bought at Amazon the ovation neoprene girth with elastic bands on one side and they are amazing for the price as the quality is excellent and very very comfortable for the horse. The only issue you may have is the sizing as if you read through the descriptions, some folks seem to see the girth being true to size and others suggest buying slightly larger.Other wonderful Amazon reviewer’s wrote me and made suggestions as far as finding the correct size if you have the saddle billets to measure from or actually taking a string and measuring the horses girth area. I didn’t take a chance and I actually bought four different sizes to make sure I found the correct size and will return the wrong sized ones. Looks like it’s a bit of a science as far as finding the right size for your horse or pony but the girth got incredible reviews and the price is exceptional for the value and the quality of the item..
text_fidelity_b: Long Western to English Leather Girth Converters

text_fidelity_a:
Fitbit Surge Fitness Superwatch, Black, Small (US Version) Original review from Nov or Dec 2015: Fitbit, my relationship with you was ruined by the zip's disapproval of my sloth-like lifestyle. The frowny faces on days I considered "high effort" were judgmental and discouraging. So, when my APNP recommended buying a Fitbit to track sleep duration/quality, I was skeptical but compliant. I was hopeful that it would provide evidence of my lack of ability to sleep. So, I purchased the Surge, which looks like a monstrous thing on my bony little wrist. For some reason, everyone thinks it is an Apple Watch. I suppose my talking to it as if it had Siri probably is part of that. Also, it lights up in the dark randomly sometimes. I think it means to do that when you lift it up to look at it but doesn't always light up when you'd think it would.

The very first day, I had to work a table at a show and got badges for effort. I felt very accomplished but moreso, I felt tired and in need of caffeine because exercise is not my thing. So imagine my surprise when the very first night, it registered screen time as sleep time. So the very meager hours I obtained appeared to be a full night's rest with one time of being awake for 20 minutes (when I went upstairs to get ready for bed). The second day was a little off as well but the Surge quickly learned. And despite accidentally whacking it against a rock at the show, not even a scratch showed up. I am impressed by its hardiness. It also has gotten wet while sweating or washing my hands and still works great, though I haven't worn it during anything like swimming or showering.

Anyway, back to data--I started using the Excel data exports on the Fitbit site and comparing it to the data I log by hand. It is now one month later and the Fitbit has become more accurate but is still not perfect. Although, to be fair, I mostly just dislike it for how it tracks the exact times I sleep and wake up, thus evidencing how often I am late for work. But that's why I bought it so I can't be too uptight about that.

So right now, I am running my own self-study on my sleeping habits to provide to my prescriber. I compare their data to the medication dosages taken, exercise, diet, etc and provide to my doctor the raw data and summaries. This affords her greater insight to change my meds accordingly. I do wish it would sync better with my chart (right now I insert the data manually from their version to the one I use) and that they would offer the options to present data in hours+minutes rather than just hours. I also wish it would offer an easy way to track heart rate patterns over long lengths of time. But I'm glad for having this data, since it helps me to improve my sleep habits and med adjustments.

I don't like is how bulky it is. It's uncomfortable to even sleep on my side such that that wrist would be under the pillow but since I use it specifically for sleep, I need to wear it all night. I also wish there was a way to charge it without taking it off. It's also strange that there doesn't seem to be a very effective way of knowing who of my Facebook Friends also has Fitbit. Right now I have maybe 10 Fitbit friends and I am the biggest sloth of all of us since I am a counselor and most of my job is sedentary. That's discouraging for the competitions and such. I need more friends who slack at exercise at my level so we can have equally matched competitions. Then I might actually start liking the exercise parts of this. Although I giggle that sometimes I can get casenoting to improve my step count since it is on my wrist.

The floors climbed thing. No. You have to increase by 10 ft of altitude or whatever to get it to count. At minimum, I have to climb one full floor of stairs per day to get to my bed. Does it count? Not reliably. Yet it seems to sometimes count when I'm driving in a hilly area, oddly enough. And as for the whole exercise activities thing, nothing to comment since I gave up the gym membership a year ago and my exercise is mostly just walking, chores, etc.

The alarms and notifications. Okay, I love that phone calls make it vibrate. I ignore my phone and always miss calls. Everything lives on silent due to work. This way I can "check my phone" during a client session without seeming obnoxious. I just wish it would display the messages of a text rather than simply that I received a text. Also, I don't like that you have to adjust the alarms via the app or Fitbit web site rather than the watch itself. And I wish you could change the intensity of the vibration. The X you have to hit on the screen to get it to stop is so tiny that if I had a stronger vibration, I would actually wake up rather than silencing all of my other 6 alarms in my sleep (I have problems, I know). That would also help my clients with hearing impairments. Also, the buttons should seem simple but are not always super intuitive. But watches aren't my thing either, so take that with a grain of salt.

Lastly, the battery life is not as long as advertised. It seems to last a couple of days. I've always had trouble with Fitbit batteries though. My Zip eats them like me with Reese's Pieces. At least the Surge is rechargeable, unlike the Zip.

The band is okay but very bulky and not super comfortable. I wish it was more customizable.

In conclusion, it's 4 stars because it is still pretty awesome, probably even moreso if you're not as lazy as me. You don't buy this because you want a smart watch. You buy it in the name of pretending you care about fitness. But it still takes up your wrist space and if it comes down to this or other smart watches, unless you really need the fitnessy stuff, you can do better. [Unless, for the non-fitness people, you are the curmudgeon type like me who says "why buy a watch for what my phone can do?" In that case, don't buy a watch. You already have a phone that can do amazing things. And if you don't, you probably know how to do things like entertain yourself without technological reliance.]

It loses one star because of its bulkiness, lack of ability to do things other watches at equal/lower prices can do (both smart and non-smart, such as the vibration levels), and non-intuitiveness. But still a solid device with as many bells and whistles as you'll get out of a Fitbit device.

*****UPDATE FEB 2016: I am downgrading this to 1 star. Not only is the thing bulky and inaccurate, it also is actually causing me arthritis-like pain on whichever wrist it was worn. I've tried loosening and tightening the strap, changing wrist placement, and several other changes and the watch is just horrible. After a couple of days without wearing it, my wrists feel healthy again. I'm not alone in this either; google it. Lots of other people are having the same issue with it causing significant pain. I wish I could return it for a full refund.
text_fidelity_b: Fitbit Surge Fitness Superwatch, Black, Small (US Version)

TITLE Gel World Full-Face Training Headgear I use this for full contact boxing sparring. By full contact I mean it's supervised mostly sparring, and we're not out to knock the other person out, but get good 70% power in strikes.

I started out with no headgear at all in sparring. Got knocked out for a good second on hook to the button.
Plenty of hits to jaws, nose, ears, etc. I felt those hits pretty good.

Then I got this headgear, since our gym started a headgear only policy if you wanted to spar.

Well I have Title Gel gloves, so I thought I'd get this headgear, as I love the gloves.
The headgear, now worn for one full session, really does lessen the blows quite a bit. You feel the hits sure enough.
But your brain doesn't get quite as scrambled, your jaw quite as well knocked around, with this well protection headgear.
I am pretty sure unless it's a real hard hit to the button, you're not going to experience a concussive knockout with this nice little piece of kit.

It does slide around on my face as I get hit, but I take a split second to straighten it out once again.

Highly recommended, I think it will save on brain injury.

text_fidelity_a: FAMELEY Camping Stove/Backpacking Stove, Portable Stainless Steel Wood Burning Stove with Nylon Carry Bag for Outdoor Hiking,Traveling and Picnic First off let me say that for the money this is a decent wood burning stove. I have used it now about 4 times and in a pinch, I am glad I have it. Positives: it works, its durable, the casing does not get super hot so you won't burn your self if you have to move it,  and it packs down small. Areas for improvement: First, I think the air flow holes/vents need to be a bit larger. After burning some wood some of the ash began to clog up the holes which did not allow good air flow. Second, (probably my biggest concern) it is difficult to keep adding fuel to this stove. Once you put the pot on top of it...it only leaves a small gap so in order to keep adding fuel you have to remove the pot for a second to add fuel so when you take the pot off the direct heat it starts to cool down. It would be nice if it had a cut out on one of the sides to be able to add wood without removing the pot. It took about 20 minutes to get a nice boil for two cups of water. So if you have time to just kick back not a big worry but if you are on the trail and want to stop for a quick lunch probably not the stove for you. Overall, I am glad I have it but probably will use it for emergencies and not so much on the trail.
text_fidelity_b: FAMELEY Camping Stove/Backpacking Stove, Portable Stainless Steel Wood Burning Stove with Nylon Carry Bag for Outdoor Hiking,Traveling and Picnic

LIGHTBAR | LED Headlamp, 300 to 500 Lumens, Spot Light Mode and Red Light Modes Available On Select Models - Perfect for Camping Running Biking Fishing Construction I've had this for a couple of months, but just used it for the first time this past weekend while camping with friends. I will never use it for that again.

A) The wide angle sounds like a good thing, but it was really annoying to my friends. I had to keep the headlamp at the lowest possible brightness, and even then the light shining so wide was still annoying to everyone around me.

B) The led strip is very thin, resulting in the light source being behind the plane of my glasses. So much light was reflecting off the lenses of my glasses back into my eyes that I truly couldn't see much of anything in front of me. There's no point lighting a path if I still can't actually see the path.

Also, this headlamp has a proprietary charger. So you have to keep that specific single-use cable with you in order to recharge the batteries. And the batteries drain even when not in use. I charged it fully when I first got it a couple of months ago. Fortunately I tested it before my camping trip and discovered it was completely drained. So you can't just charge it and expect it to be ready when you need it. I had to fully charge it just before I left.

It is really very bright, so if you need something really bright, and you don't have glasses, and there's no one else around you who might be blinded by your headlight, then it might be an ok choice for you. But with so very many options out there, I recommend you keep looking. There are definitely better choices than this.
text_fidelity_b: LIGHTBAR | LED Headlamp, 300 to 500 Lumens, Spot Light Mode and Red Light Modes Available On Select Models - Perfect for Camping Running Biking Fishing Construction

Unfortunately, road vibrations cause the light to shut off. Before I gave up on this light, I tried to keep it on by checking every 10-15 seconds on my 20-minute ride to work. I had to turn the light back on at least 20 times. So aggravating! At least the crappy $10 lights stay on!

I give it 2 stars due to Fortified's stellar customer service. I wrote them about the issue and they mailed me some rubber bumpers to help hold the battery inside the housing. The reason the light shorts out is because the battery slides loosely into a chamber with the light bulb connection at the base. Amazingly minor road vibrations break the battery-bulb connection and the light shuts off, and doesn't come back on.

Fortified has refunded my purchase, which I really appreciate. I believe there is a chance I received a defective product. I cannot say this for sure, as I was offered rubber bumpers instead of a full replacement.

Check one of these out at your local bike shop, and make sure they have a refund policy.

Sometimes the razor is just too sharp for my preference. For this reason, I held off on purchasing one, but used my friends somewhat regularly on hunting trips.

Right after I heard that the double-bladed version was out, I jumped on it. This thing is exactly what I wanted out of a skinning knife. I can switch between the razor and the heavier blade quickly and don't have to keep track of 2 knives. It's not very large and not even that heavy. Given all that and the price, I must say that I am pretty happy with it. I did my first deer with this knife shortly after I purchased it and am really happy with it.

text_fidelity_a:
Gosky 20-60x80 Dual Focusing ED Spotting Scope - Ultra High Definition Optics Scope with Carrying Case and Smartphone Adapter for Target Shooting Hunting Bird Watching Wildlife Astronomy Scenery I have a house with a fantastic view, including a field about 1000 yards off that is visited by majestic Roosevelt elk, and an airport about 4 miles out. My trusty pair of Leupold 8x binos really don't provide enough up-closeness for those sorts of distances. I tried a pair of BARSKA Gladiator 20-140x80 Zoom Binoculars, but was disappointed by two things: First, I'm no optician, but I really don't think the BARSKA is capable of 140x zoom. At the highest magnification, the image was no more zoomed than on this Gosky (actually, pretty sure the Gosky is more powerful). Second, at higher magnifications the BARSKA's images were murky and cloudy. (Other people using the BARSKAs say that the two eyes don't align very well -- but there's supposed to be an adjustment for that.) I liked the binocular depth perception of the Gosky, which was (surprisingly) apparent even at several hundred yards. But with the Gosky I got a much brighter and crisper view. (Also, for really distant objects, like the moon, I'm pretty sure that binocularity is lost anyway because the angle created by the separation of your eyes becomes insignificant at some point.)
I definitely appreciate the advantages of getting a (not included) lightweight tripod with this 'scope. The weight of the Gosky is considerable, and the magnification amplifies any movements. Put it on a tripod, and those issues are solved.
I have been using the Gosky spotting scope for animal- and birdwatching, plane-spotting, landmark finding, and looking at the surface of the moon. I can even pick out the ball and the plays when the kids play baseball in the field about 2 miles off.
I'm sure there are many more expensive, better made, connoisseur-quality optics out there, but the Gosky suits my needs and abilities just fine at this point.
text_fidelity_b: Gosky 20-60x80 Dual Focusing ED Spotting Scope - Ultra High Definition Optics Scope with Carrying Case and Smartphone Adapter for Target Shooting Hunting Bird Watching Wildlife Astronomy Scenery

text_fidelity_a:
Yes4All Versatile Wooden Wobble Balance Trainer Board with 360 Degree Rotation I love this amazing balance board. I've tried out quite a few balance boards, and this one is the absolute best of this style. The thing that I like most about it is that it's very comfortable to use when I just have my bare feet. I mostly use it with shoes, but I really like that I have the option of using it with just bare feet.

The whole surface has a grip coating. It's kind of like what they have on skateboards, but like I said, this is much more comfortable to stand on with your bare feet. If you're super uncoordinated like me, then you might be wondering if you should wait until you're stronger to start working on your balance. But, I totally recommend this to be one the first pieces of fitness equipment that you get. The biggest reason is that it's pretty easy to balance on, and when you're balancing then you generally aren't locking your knees, which is the biggest reason why beginners get injured.

The other thing that I really like about this is that the bottom is smooth. This might not seem like a very important feature, but with this style of balance board, it actually is, because all of your weight gets concentrated into a very tiny area on the floor. If the bottoms of these aren't smooth, they will indent even the hardest of floors. So, because it has a smooth bottom, then it makes it perfect to use on almost any surface. True, it does slip just a tiny bit, over a grip surface, but I don't mind a little slipping because it's supposed to be teaching me balance.

The construction of this is great. It's about seven layers of board, stuck together. The bottom is an extremely firmly secured piece of very sturdy plastic. Overall, this is an awesome balance board. It's awesome for beginners like me, but if you're already a fitness expert and in awesome shape, then I really think you'll like it too.

*Yes4All gave me this board to review*
text_fidelity_b: Yes4All Versatile Wooden Wobble Balance Trainer Board with 360 Degree Rotation

MSR Dromedary Bag Water Reservoir With a chronic migraine that hasn’t gone away in years, I’ve slept with a block of ice as the upper half of my pillow for almost as long. It’s just one of the things that really help.

Now, having a container that’ll stay ice cold all night without peeing the bed, that can be a challenge. These are the most durable water bladders I’ve found, and after a year of being frozen and thawed every day, filled to about 85-90% with a little room left for expansion, they show absolutely no real signs of wear. They’ve gotten dirty, and I’ve had to scrub them now and then, but they are very reliable. My only issue has been the tiny nozzle on the little cap, which will occasionally pop open and cause problems. That’s easily fixed with a piece of duct tape. Considering what I put these things through, I really couldn’t imagine finding a better alternative.

It would be nice if they could make the fabric covering a smoother texture, but honestly, that’s a particularly nit-picky detail that most people using these for intended purposes, couldn’t care less about.

These things last so long, if you don’t lose them and you’re not using them in active military service, I seriously doubt you’ll need to replace them for a long time to come. I bet if I’d had one while I was in the army, I’d still be using it. They’re far tougher than the 2-quart canteens I was issued, that’s for sure.
text_fidelity_b: MSR Dromedary Bag Water Reservoir

text_fidelity_a: SUNLITE Unicycle Cotterless Steel Crank Arm Set, Silver The first unicycle I had was in Germany when I was with the US Army in Heidelberg. It was a VERY hard to ride 26 or 28 inch. Not a good one to learn on. Changing it to a 24 inch by rebuilding the wheel (but keeping the same long cranks) made it much easier to ride. That was in 1983 and that unicycle has since worn out. (I rode it a LOT, all over the World!) But newer unicycles lacked the same quality of that ride and the "feel" was all wrong. I didn't even know that cranks came in different lengths in 1983, but reducing the large wheel diameter while keeping the 6 inch cranks is what made the ride so nice. (With shorter cranks it's not as easy to balance or pedal, and you go too fast- not impossible but not as much fun.) Proof of that came with these 6 inch SUNLITE cotterless cranks which changed the performance of a 24 inch that came with 5 inch cranks to finding that "sweet spot" it had been missing. They're very heavy and strong, I doubt I'll be able to bend these.
text_fidelity_b: SUNLITE Unicycle Cotterless Steel Crank Arm Set, Silver

Even that tent took me a minute to learn the best and fastest way to put it together, so y'know, everything new is a bit of a learning experience, right?  Now, for the tent - I love the roominess of it and how I can arrange my stuff so that I have the most standing space when walking in/out/around the tent.  I have a 10" twin air mattress with an internal pump so once I had this tent set up and my bed was fully-inflated, bringing in the cooler, a small table, hanging a solar lamp - I was done within an hour and man, I had one heck of a good-looking camping set up!  Of course, just looking good isn't the point.  It was hot that first day, but with a clip on solar fan moving air inside the tent was not bad at all, plus the mesh front and back flaps allow good air movement.  I'm very happy with the tent itself, but I wish this had come with a separate "awning" - it didn't need to be attached.  Maybe backing up your SUV, using the open back for holding two ends and poles to hold the other two ends so you have a sheltered space outside the tent for relaxing (out of the sun or rain) would be appreciated.  Other than that, this is an excellent tent.

text_fidelity_a: Schwinn Twinn Classic Tandem Adult Beach Cruiser Bike, Double Seater, Steel Low Step Frame, 7-Speed, 650c Urban Tires, Alloy Caliper Brakes, Medium Frame, Blue As seniors, it became difficult to mount our current tandem, so decided to replace it with the blue Schwinn because it was advertised as a low step frame suitable for a captain 5'6" to 6'1" (I am 5'10").  It was also advertised as having 26" tires.  Upon receipt, we found shipping box was punctured and seemed to be mishandled, but contents seemed to look ok.  After assembly, found front chain cover and pedal cranks badly scratched.  Also, found it very difficult to mount for both "captain and stoker".  Upon inspection, found the tires were 27.5" and not 26".  However, decided to just ask for a replacement chain cover. Thus, advise checking tire size before assembling, especially if "captain" is under 5'10".  Finally, the bike was made in China, so basically paying for the  name.
